Prayer:

Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution o  India, praying this Court to issue a Writ of Mandamus, to direct th  respondents to ensure that the edible oil sold in the market are in  accordance with FSSI standards and norms and to take appropriate  action on those who are flouting these rules and to take severe pen  action on the traders who are involved in adulteration and  misbranding or in anyway affecting the standard norms and  conditions of FSSI Act and regulations.

For Petitioner : Mr.T.Dinesh  for M/s.Veera Associat  For Respondent-1 : Mr.G.Rajaraman  For RR2 to 5 : Mr.P.Thilakkumar  Government Pleader S.Arunnithy vs The Chief Executive Officer on 29 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11878742/
2  For R6 : Mr.B.Saravanan  Senior Counsel  assisted by Mr.M.Rajar  2/7
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 04:04:49 pm )

 
 ORDER
[Order of the Court was made by S.M.SUBRAMANIAM, J.]

The writ on hand has been instituted seeking direction to the respondents to ensure that the edible oil sold in the market are in accordance with FSSI standards and norms and to take appropriate action on those who are flouting the rules and to take severe penal action on the traders who are involved in adulteration and misbranding or in anyway affecting the standard norms and conditions of FSSI Act and regulations.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that adulterated edible oil is being sold in open market, which would result in health hazards and thus, the present Public Interest Litigation came to be instituted.
3. It is brought to the notice of this Court that during the relevant point of time, when the writ petition was pending, sale of edible oil in loose was permitted and subsequently, it was prohibited by the order of the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, dated 18.08.2020.

For better appreciation, the scanned copy of the order dated 18.08.2020 is reproduced hereunder:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 04:04:49 pm )

4. In view of the prohibition imposed by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration,
no further consideration is required in respect of the relief sought for in the present writ petition.
Consequently, this Writ Petition stands disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.

[S.M.S., J.] 
 J.]
